headline: Saudi Arabia Expands Oil Storage Rights in Japan Under Supply Deal
summary: Japan plans to buy up to 8 million barrels of Saudi crude oil to restock national petroleum reserves drawn down during the Hormuz crisis. The agreement grants Saudi Arabia an additional 16 million barrels of storage capacity in Japan.
why: Saudi Arabia is the world's top crude oil exporter, while Japan relies heavily on Middle Eastern energy imports to meet domestic demand.

impacts.name: Brent Crude
impacts.why: Japan agreed to purchase up to 8 million barrels of crude oil from Saudi Arabia to rebuild strategic reserves.
